title: VIII–XI. Eves fourfold penalty; natural and spiritual state after the fall
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): it stands as partly ye loss belonging toward Gods first grace plus favor, partly — what followed this — ye grieving belonging toward Gods good Spirit plus His departure out from ye human, that same which continuously ye darkness belonging toward mind plus ignorance or crookedness belonging toward will followed, plus ye disturbance, perversity, plus sinister turn belonging toward all ye affections — as to ye spiritual state. ye force belonging toward nature was loosed plus left to itself, plus stands as no longer ruled plus repressed by means belonging toward that same peculiar providence belonging toward God by means belonging toward that same which under ye state belonging toward innocence it was held back lest it bring any trouble on humans, as we taught above — as to ye natural state. XI. the curse belonging toward ye ground, labor in sweat, return to dust. Adams penalty: desire toward ye husband, ye husbands rule, plus death — multiplication belonging toward pain in childbirth. EVES penalty has four parts: VIII.
pass_b_english: VIII. EVES penalty has four parts: multiplication of pain in childbirth, desire toward the husband, the husbands rule, and death. Adams penalty: the curse of the ground, labor in sweat, return to dust.

XI. As to the natural state, the force of nature was loosed and left to itself, and is no longer ruled and repressed by that peculiar providence of God by which under the state of innocence it was held back lest it bring any trouble on humans, as we taught above. As to the spiritual state, it is partly the loss of Gods first grace and favor, partly — what followed this — the grieving of Gods good Spirit and His departure from the human, which continuously the darkness of mind and ignorance or crookedness of will followed, and the disturbance, perversity, and sinister turn of all the affections.
source_text: VIII. EVAE quatuor habet partes poena: multiplicatio doloris in partu, desiderium ad virum, dominatio viri, et mors. Adami poena: maledictio terrae, labor in sudore, reditus in pulverem. XI. Quantum ad statum naturalem, soluta sibi permissa est vis naturae, nec amplius peculiari illa Dei providentia qua sub statu innocentiae regitur ac reprimitur, qua videlicet ne molestiae quicquam hominibus inferret cohibebatur, ut supra docuimus. Quantum ad statum spiritualem est partim amissio primae DEI gratiae et faventiae, partim, quae hanc secuta est, boni Dei Spiritus contristatio et ab homine discessio, quam continenter excepit mentis caligo et agnoia seu voluntatis obliquitas, affectuumque omnium perturbatio, perversitas et sinistra.
